articleTitle: Optimization of Hyperspectral Image Classification Using Monte Carlo-Based Band Reduction
abstract: Hyperspectral images are the concatenation of images taken at different wavelengths with a very narrow bandwidth, from ultraviolet to mid-infrared. These different images are combined into a hypercube structure of very large size, which contains much more information than classical RGB images. One of the drawbacks of using a hyperspectral camera is the time it takes to acquire a hypercube, up to few minutes. However, it's easy to see that to detect a particular feature in a hypercube, only a part of the wavelengths are needed, allowing the use of multispectral cameras i.e. only a reduced set of wavelengths, acquired at the same speed as RGB cameras. The choice of wavelengths to capture depends on the detection required, in our case the segmentation of the image. Therefore, this paper focuses on the use of the Monte Carlo method to find the best wavelengths needed, and the use of a form of unsupervised classification through the clustering method k-means to evaluate the results. Multiple simulations were performed using the Monte Carlo method to select the wavelengths and several metrics were defined to compare the results between using all the wavelengths and using only a few of them.

articleTitle: Regression Analysis of Factors Affecting Round-Trip Regenerative Braking Efficiency Using Real-World Data
abstract: Regenerative braking is an effective way of improving the overall efficiency of electrified road vehicles. When driving, as well as optimising the strategy, it is important to understand the main factors affecting the energy recuperated in the real-world, both positively and negatively. A series of over 60 drives in both directions between Swieqi, Malta, and the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Malta were performed, on different days, in different conditions, on a 2017 Nissan LEAF AZE-0. A multiple linear regression study with threefold validation was performed for each direction, taking the round-trip regenerative braking efficiency as the dependent variable. When eliminating outliers, a model with an absolute mean error of less than 5 per cent was achieved. The trip between Swieqi and the Faculty of Engineering is predominantly downhill, while the return is predominantly uphill. It was found that downhill, the main factors influencing the round-trip regenerative efficiency were brake pressure and vehicle speed. Uphill, however, the regenerative braking efficiency was mostly influenced by the torque. It was therefore concluded that the independent variables of brake pressure, vehicle speed, and motor torque can capture the regenerative braking efficiency successfully for such routes. Considering input and output motor torque, the average round-trip regenerative braking efficiency was found to be 50.1 per cent.

articleTitle: Automation-Driven Dataset Preparation for Continuous Czech Sign Language Recognition
abstract: This paper presents an automation-driven solution for preparing a continuous Czech Sign Language dataset, addressing the lack of resources in this area. Manual processing of daily sign language news recordings would be extremely time-consuming, as the videos vary in quality, use different overlays, and have no captions. To streamline this process, we use the Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) to compare key frames and extract relevant parts of the recording, such as weather forecast segments. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) then processes the accompanying audio and generates textual transcriptions of the spoken content. The outcome is the highly automated preparation pipeline and the dataset containing 4699 annotated videos of weather forecast news in Czech Sign Language providing a foundation for future research in sign language recognition.

articleTitle: Novel Concept for Automated Charging of Professional Electric Vehicle Fleets
abstract: Automated charging of electric car fleets has great potential to improve effectiveness of charging infrastructure. The development of an automated charging system for company vehicle fleets requires new approaches for realizing both, safe and convenient charging processes as well as efficient fleet and charging management. In this context, the present paper introduces a novel concept for automated charging of electric vehicles by use of a specifically developed robotic system. The charging station is combined with a comprehensive fleet- and charging management system to enable effective application within company environment. The system has been built on enhanced prototype level for testing under real life conditions to evaluate the potential of the technology.

articleTitle: Torque Improvement Method for Flux Modulated Motor by Inserting Magnets Between Pole Pieces
abstract: This paper proposes a torque improvement method for a flux modulated motor with magnetic modulation. This motor consists of an inner stator with permanent magnets, a rotor with pole pieces, and an outer stator with coils. We investigated the possibility of improving the torque by inserting permanent magnets into the air space between the pole pieces. As a result, it was theoretically clarified that the torque can be greatly improved under certain conditions.

articleTitle: Complete Kinematic Analysis of the Joint Variables of the Robot Mechanism During the End-Effector's Movement Along a Circular Path
abstract: This article explores the kinematic analysis of the component movements within a robotic mechanism, focusing specifically on joint movements as the “end effector” traverses a circular trajectory. The primary aim is to introduce a methodology for performing a comprehensive kinematic analysis of the robot's open kinematic chain. The end effector's path within the multi-link manipulator model is defined using a 5th-degree polynomial, creating a circular trajectory. Calculations involve determining the angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular acceleration as the effector progresses along the circle. Furthermore, all six kinematic relationships are defined with respect to time and interdependence. The shape of the workspace is derived under varying angular constraints alongside the outlined trajectory of the end effector. When the arm reaches maximum extension, the patterns of angular rotation, angular velocity, and angular acceleration are specified. Matlab software is used to obtain and analyze these results.

articleTitle: StateFlow as a Tool of the Hybrid X-in-the-Loop Technique in the Model-Based Design Approach to the Control Systems Design in Industrial Automation
abstract: The rapid dynamics of changes in the definition of requirements when deploying new technologies means an increase in demands on the volume and scope of skills and knowledge of experts in the design of solutions and their implementation. PLC-based control systems designed for industrial automation can also be included in this problem area. The article deals with the possibility of rapid design and testing of PLC control algorithms using X-in-the-Loop techniques of Model-based Design approach. The control algorithm is implemented using visual programming techniques in the form of state diagrams utilizing the Matlab StateFlow tool. The given proposal is analyzed from the point of view of different approaches to the implementation of communication between the development PC and the real control PLC SIMATIC S7-300 connected to the real part of the model production line. Data exchange is carried out in two ways. The first way of communication is the exchange of uncompressed and compressed images of inputs and outputs via IP communication. The second way is to use the OPC UA architecture. The result of the article is a case study of the use of the XiL approach in the design phase of the control of the AFB Factory production line module with a summary of the possibilities, advantages and disadvantages of alternative partial solutions.

articleTitle: Vertical Stabilization of Bipedal Walking Drone PAVO with Proximal Policy Optimization
abstract: While autonomous mobile robots have gained more popularity over the last few years and many traditional problems (such as navigation and locomotion) seem to have been solved with an adequate level of accuracy, walking and biped robots still face many challenges. We present an approach to the stabilization of mobile robots with two legs, which move via quasi-dynamic movement. A popular machine learning method, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), was used to learn how to stabilize the robot in a vertical position. This method is popular for solving complex problem domains with high-dimensional state-action spaces and continuous states and actions, which are common in areas involving walking robots with a high number of degrees of freedom. The method was tested on a custom-designed biped walking robot, PAVO.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Remote-Control System for Building Lighting Management
abstract: The global landscape of electric energy is shaped by various factors, including technological advancements, increasing energy demand, climate change, political decisions, and economic conditions. Many countries face challenges in their energy sectors, such as shortages and rising costs, which can impede economic growth. These issues stem from heightened energy demands linked to economic development, limited transmission capacities, and unexpected events like natural disasters. In response, there is a global shift towards renewable energy sources-such as hydropower, wind, solar, and geothermal-as alternatives to fossil fuels, supported by sustainability-focused innovations aimed at efficient energy production and distribution. The authors have developed a lighting control system to enhance energy efficiency and operational effectiveness within its facilities. This system's design prioritizes user comfort by eliminating the need for individuals to reach switches to control lighting physically. It also incorporates automated features that enhance energy savings by ensuring lights are only on when needed. The extensible nature of the system allows for future expansions, including monitoring the status of devices within the building and receiving notifications for error messages. This initiative exemplifies the authors' commitment to energy conservation and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of Current Measurement Circuit Using PCB Rogowski Coils for Resonant Converters
abstract: Measuring current in a resonant tank of the resonant converters requires fast response and low interference for resonant circuits. For this purpose, a current measurement circuit with PCB based Rogowski coil was designed. The individual circuit parts and characteristics are described. The circuit test results on an LLC resonant converter and double pulse test are provided as well.

articleTitle: Usage and Added Value of IO-Link Platform in the Context of Industry 4.0
abstract: The paper analyses and practically verifies the principles of Industry 4.0 through an IoT approach based explicitly on IO-Link technology. The focus is on the definition of appropriate data and the determination of the communication topology. By creating an initial knowledge base, we document the implementation of advanced monitoring, the ability to make future predictions about the state and condition of individual connected devices, and the automated workplace. Our experiments, setup, and data collection demonstrate the effectiveness of implementing the presented approach in other typo-logically similar workplaces. Thus, from the results obtained and their comprehensive evaluation of the collected data, we documented not only the applicability of our solution but also the transfer of knowledge to other industrial areas.

articleTitle: Seven-Level Transformerless Inverter with a Double Boost Controlled Cell
abstract: This paper presents a new high-voltage gain single-phase seven-level Boost inverter topology with reduced harmonic distortion. The proposed solution introduces a transformerless multilevel voltage source inverter with reduced number of passive and active power components using only a single input DC power source. The maximum voltage gain is three times higher than the input power source. The circuit is composed by a double boost controlled cell using a single power device where both inductors suppress the capacitors current charge spikes. The proposed topology is verified under different conditions, and the some simulation and experimental results are presented, considering a 300 W laboratory prototype model.

articleTitle: Design of a Data Collection Layer for Complementary Diagnostic and Condition Monitoring System of a Robotic Workplace
abstract: The core of this contribution is the design of a system for the identification of parameters and preliminary diagnostics of a robotic workplace based on the collected data from additive sensors. As the physical device for testing is a robotic workplace on the Festo AFB Factory automated production line is used. The goal of the proposed solution is to provide a complementary image of the state of the industrial workplace, through the additional sensory layer created. The first part of the publication is focused on data collection, considering the suitability of the data and the evaluation of the parameters necessary for the operability of the device. In addition, the key parameters for the predictive maintenance process are identified, and a method of further processing and evaluation of values is suggested. The proposed data collection layer is part of the planned predictive maintenance system that significantly improves the reliability of the designated workplace. The final solution offers the ability to react to device malfunctions in real time and correct/improve its condition with timely intervention.

articleTitle: Additional Losses in the Winding Under Higher Frequency Current
abstract: This paper explores the additional losses in electrical machine windings, focusing on high-frequency operations. These losses arise from the skin effect, proximity effect, and circulating currents within the winding conductors. The selected loss-suppressing methods are demonstrated using a stator stack for a small permanent magnet synchronous motor with a fractional-slot concentrated winding. Selected winding configurations are manually wound and the measurements are compared with the finite element method. Core losses are measured independently.

articleTitle: Integrated Monitoring of Stress and Damage Using CNN Deep Learning of Electromechanical Impedance Responses of CSA Sensor
abstract: A multitask 2D CNN model is designed for integrated monitoring stress and damage in concrete specimens utilizing the raw impedance signatures of capsule-like smart aggregated (CSA). The fundamental theory of CSA-based EMI method is presented to describe how the sensor responds to compressive loads. Next, compression tests on a CSA-embedded concrete cylinder are conducted to record the stress-damage EMI responses of CSA sensor under applied stresses. The multitask 2D CNN model learned the impedance signals for predicting the concrete stress and damage is constructed. Consequently, the generalization and robustness of the developed model are tested against noise and untrained data.

articleTitle: Design of an Active Seat Suspension Based on the Kempe Mechanism
abstract: The paper presents a cost-effective design of an active seat suspension intended to be tested on an existing car seat shaker test rig. The active seat suspension is based on the Kempe mechanism, is suitable for low-cost mass production, and aims to enhance passenger comfort with an emphasis on autonomous vehicle applications. The system is designed based on the requirements gained through computer simulations of active-seat suspension-equipped vehicles and the dimensions that correspond to the rigid suspension seat typically employed in B-segment passenger vehicles. The proposed design includes four main subsystems: (i) carrier based on Kempe straight line linkage mechanism, (ii) actuator based on the spindle, rotational servomotor, and rhomboidal set of levers, (iii) set of four torsional springs, and (iv) adjustable damper.

articleTitle: Optimal Parameters Choice for Synchronous Reluctance Machines
abstract: The paper describes a procedure for optimal parameters choice for synchronous reluctance machines in terms of maximization of machine power factor and overloadability. The analytical calculations are verified by finite element method models of two selected design variations.

articleTitle: Iron Loss in Multiphase Machines
abstract: The calculation of iron loss in electrical machines is a vast subject and their exact determination is a very complex matter due to the number of variables. The literature dealing with machine design is mainly focused on three-phase machines and thus assumes harmonic magnetic flux waveforms. Due to harmonic injection, magnetic flux deformations occur, and standard computational methods cannot be used. Therefore, this paper focuses on the calculation of magnetic flux variations due to harmonic injection in the individual parts of a nine-phase induction machine and further describes the effect of these variations on hysteresis loss and eddy current loss.

articleTitle: Ellipse Fitting with a Dual Kalman Filter for an Adaptive Angle Tracking Observer
abstract: We present an ellipse fitting approach with a dual Kalman filter to realize an adaptive angle tracking observer (ATO), suitable for actuator motion control. In many applications where resolvers are used to sense angular displacements, the control system has high requirements for accuracy and fast dynamics. However, harsh environmental conditions and the usage of low-cost sensors impose challenges, as parameters are prone to drift, e.g. due to temperature variations or aging. The proposed ATO utilizes two estimators, one for fast state estimation and another for resolver parameter tracking. The resolvers characteristic is described geometrically with an ellipse, and we demonstrate how its parameters can be fitted online along with their uncertainty ranges. Experiments with simulated and real data from a brake-by-wire actuator show satisfying state and parameter estimation performance, which we also compare to a baseline gradient descent algorithm. The proposed adaptive ATO design, with its simple architecture built upon established state estimation tools, is attractive for various applications that use mechatronic actuators.

articleTitle: Control Strategy of Buck and Boost Converters Using MATLAB Software
abstract: DC/ DC converters are used to convert the DC voltage from one level to another level. The topologies are like a buck converter which steps down the voltage and boost converter which step up the voltage level. There will be electromagnetic interference due to high switching frequencies in the dc converters. In this paper, the Buck converter and Boost converter using different types of controllers like PI and PID controllers are modelled. The model is designed using MATLAB Simulink. The proportional integral controller is used to decrease the steady state error without affecting the stability of the control system. The proportional integral derivative controller is used to improve the stability of the control system and to decrease steady state errors. The use of these controllers for the buck and Boost converter modelling gives a significant change in the error for a variable load of 10–1000 ohms to achieve a constant output voltage. This will be presented in the paper how these controllers will affect the converters. The load used in this converter is resistive.

articleTitle: Kinematic Analysis and Torque Dynamics of a 5-DOF Robotic Manipulator for Enhanced Precision and Fault Detection in FDM 3D Printing
abstract: This paper comprehensively analyzes a 5-DOF robotic manipulator, focusing on kinematics, Jacobian matrix derivation, singularity characterization, and torque computation. The study enhances precision and efficiency in robotic operations through advanced modeling and simulation techniques. Key contributions include detailed insights into the kinematics, torque dynamics, and singularity analysis of the manipulator, guiding the design of robots for computer vision tasks in FDM 3D printing. Illustrating singularity regions and optimizing trajectory planning offer a basic framework for ensuring compatibility across various 3D printers, advancing robotic design, and improving quality assurance in additive manufacturing.

articleTitle: Digital Twin for CNC Machine Tools Design
abstract: This paper describes a systematic approach to creating a digital twin, which is focused on the design stage of the product lifecycle of a production machine, considering its operating conditions. To monitor the machine's operating condition in real time, the production machine is linked with a processing environment represented by ANSYS software. The system is demonstrated by evaluating the suitability of the headstock design of a CNC machine tool in terms of stress and strain analysis when it is operated under different performance conditions. First, a model of the machine headstock is created, which is then optimized for FEM calculations with fast response and loading forces obtained from direct dynamometer measurements. It was found that the proposed “design” digital twin approach can be used to optimize other structural elements of production machines based on realistic operating conditions that reflect the operation of machines in different technological sectors.

articleTitle: Integrating Mechatronics Principles in Modern Air Defence Systems
abstract: Mechatronics, as an interdisciplinary scientific branch, offers innovative solutions to the complex challenges faced by air defence systems. This article explores the key mechatronics principles applied in the development and optimisation of air defence technologies, including sensor integration, real-time data processing, automated targeting, and intelligent control systems. By leveraging these principles, modern air defence systems achieve superior accuracy in threat detection, tracking, and interception, thereby improving overall defensive capabilities. The synergy between mechatronics and air defence not only enhances operational effectiveness but also reduces response times and increases technical reliability. This comprehensive paper underscores the transformative impact of mechatronics on air defence, highlighting case studies and real-world applications that demonstrate its critical role in ensuring national security in an era of rapidly evolving aerial threats. The paper provides a general overview of SBAD and mechatronics applications and focuses in more detail on the example of missile guidance using the Track via Missile principle and proportional guidance method.

articleTitle: 2D Finite Element Modeling and Analysis of Single-Turn Coil Configuration in Magnetic Spring Energy Harvester
abstract: This paper investigates a magnetic spring energy harvester configuration with single-turn coil to increase the electrical performance. This nonlinear energy harvester that converts vibration into useful electric power consists of an oscillating levitated magnet in-between two stationary magnets. The magnetic interaction with single-turn coil and magnetic spring energy harvester is analyzed in an experimental evaluation and using the 2D finite element method (FEM). Therefore the configuration of magnetic spring and multi-turn electric coil is simulated in 2D FEM to achieve the coil size and number of turns. This study can provide the geometric design parameters and performance of magnetic spring energy harvester based on multi-turn coil.

articleTitle: Design of a Device for Automatic Evaluation of the Level of Individual Perception of Sensory Stimuli
abstract: This research presents an improved device that can simplify and refine the assessment of individual sensory perception, specifically stereognosia. The device automates the entire assessment process, removing the subjectivity and potential errors associated with manual methods and providing a more accurate, consistent and reliable assessment. Key features of the device include automated data acquisition, efficient data processing and analysis, and enhanced reliability. Automated data acquisition ensures accurate and precise measurement of test results without human intervention, minimizing the risk of errors and improving the overall consistency of the evaluation. Efficient data processing and analysis capabilities enable rapid and comprehensive analysis of test data, facilitating the identification of patterns, trends, and individual differences in sensory perception. The device is designed to help advance the diagnosis and treatment of sensory disorders. By providing a more objective and reliable assessment of sensory function, it can help identify early signs of sensory dysfunction, monitor treatment progress and develop targeted interventions.

articleTitle: Energy-Aware Adaptive QoS Algorithm for IoT
abstract: Today, energy management systems represent a cornerstone of every embedded system, especially in IoT devices, which have become a fundamental part of our lives in this digitalized world. Many researchers have focused on using EMS to conserve energy and extend the lifetime of IoT devices. We chose a different approach to provide more energy, thereby prolonging the operational lifetime of IoT devices and enhancing their QoS parameters. This approach is based on providing an energy-aware management system that adapts the QoS based on a machine learning model predicting the available solar energy hourly, which led to extending the operational lifetime of the IoT device by approximately 300 %, the QoS in terms of active duty cycle by 400 %, and transmission power strength by 200 %.

articleTitle: Applying Artificial Intelligence Methods to Identify Selected Cybersecurity Problems in Computer Networks
abstract: The article presents the possibilities of using artificial intelligence to identify cybersecurity problems in computer networks. The research focused on developing advanced AI techniques to detect attacks quickly and accurately and respond in real-time. The tests included a detailed analysis of selected machine learning algorithms, neural networks, genetic algorithms, and behavioral analysis. The described methods were implemented and tested on a real dataset, evaluating their effectiveness, efficiency, and usability. The results will be used to develop optimal AI solutions for identifying cybersecurity problems.

articleTitle: IoT Approach Implementation Based on Flexible and Robust Node-RED Platform for Workplace Digitisation Increasing
abstract: The interoperability and connectivity of automated workplace devices are currently critical factors for their digitisation when introducing IoT approaches. The advent of flexible and robust platforms, such as Node-RED, is the main supporting element of data transfer between technologically different devices. The article is therefore oriented towards implementing this approach with an emphasis on testing, verification, and visualization of data from various devices through a server on Raspberry Pi. Innovation of the presented approach lies in designing and constructing seamless communication between typologically different industrial automation devices. The authors' motivation was explicitly to verify the requirements and demands of practice through available research capabilities. The goal is to analyze the speed and reliability of communication and, at the same time, evaluate the use of this approach in actual practice conditions. However, the experimental results of the collected and relevant data already demonstrate the platform's viability and point to the future need for network optimization and the configuration of its devices.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Modeling of Compressor Characteristics
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to modeling a turbojet engine compressor through the approximation and interpolation of performance characteristics. A hybrid method is proposed, fitting each speed line individually with the most suitable function from a predefined library of candidate functions. To address the ill-conditioning issue, a modified <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> interpolation method is introduced. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> curves are carefully defined to ensure that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> grid remains entirely within the map, avoiding extrapolation. Each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> curve is defined by a set of control points given by its intersections with speed lines, and an optimization problem is formulated to evenly distribute these points along the speed line. The resulting control points are parametrized for each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> curve, allowing for a coordinate transform that facilitates well-behaved nonlinear interpolation.

articleTitle: Operational Environment Impact on Sensor Capabilities in Special Purpose Unmanned Ground Vehicles
abstract: Unmanned platforms are increasingly used in environments where human presence is restricted including military operations, disaster response, and remote exploration. The autonomous or semi-autonomous functioning of these vehicles is related to the perception system, which incorporate a range of sensors such as LIDAR, cameras, radar, and inertial measurement units (IMUs). However, dense vegetation poses significant challenges to object detection and recognition, introducing issues such as occlusion and signal distortion caused by foliage. This study presents the limitations of both active sensors (LIDAR, radar) and passive sensors (cameras) under adverse weather conditions and security concerns on the sensing capabilities of special-purpose UGVs

articleTitle: Modeling & Analysis of Quantum Confinement and Ballistic Transport Phenomena in 3D FinFET
abstract: This research paper describes the modeling and analysis of quantum confinement of carriers and the ballistic transport phenomenon in advanced 3D FinFET structure. We use Bohm Quantum Potential (BQP) model to perform modeling, simulations and to study the quantum confinement of carrier density in advanced 3D FinFET device. During the ballistic phenomenon, carrier moves without any collision and scattering across the channel of the device. Non-Equilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) is discussed for the computation of ballistic IV curves. 3D comparison of drift-diffusion and Non Equilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) models for nanoscale FinFET is performed and quantum confinement in FinFET channel is presented. We used the advanced structure of silicon FinFET having thickness 6x7nm and gate length of 30nm to investigate the quantum confinement of carriers and to compare the Non Equilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) and classical drift diffusion models.

articleTitle: Case Study of Robot Machining at Different Working Space Locations
abstract: Machining, 3d printing and robot welding require a minimum difference between simulated and real position of robot (TCP) to facilitate high quality surface finish and fulfil dimension and form tolerance. The solution is the absolute robot calibration, which increases positional accuracy. In this paper, a calibrated direct-measuring robot is used to machine the sample part. In the experiment, the sample part is positioned at different location and machined by different machining processes. Then the produced part is measured on a coordinate measuring machine (CMM). The quality of the surface finish, dimensions and geometric tolerances are evaluated. This experiment showed the effect of calibration on the machining process. Based on the obtained results, further activities will be directed in the field of increasing the geometric accuracy of industrial robots.

articleTitle: Modal Properties Tuning Analysis of Dynamic System with Piezoelectric Components
abstract: This paper explores the modal properties tuning of mechanical systems using piezoelectric transducers. The study focuses on piezoelectric shunt damping techniques, particularly Synchronous Switch Damping on Voltage (SSDV), to mitigate vibration and alter resonant frequencies. Simulations and experiments were conducted to investigate the influence of phase shifts and applied voltage on the system's dynamics. The simulation results indicate significant changes in the resonant frequency at certain phase shifts, while the experimental results showed partial alignment with the simulations, revealing challenges in electronics and the need for precise control. This research contributes to the development of adaptive vibration control technologies, enhancing the stability and lifespan of mechanical systems.

articleTitle: Automated Production Data Integration and Processing via Simulation Based Digital Twin
abstract: Recent developments in the production sector are slowly beginning to test Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) and their ability to compete with the remainder of the market, especially the enterprises specializing in large-scale mass production. The ever-increasing demand gradually creates a large gap between the various competitors and often forces the SME to take risks when making important decisions regarding production control. One of the solutions to this problem can be the use of a simulation based Digital Twin (DT) as a decisionmaking tool for production control. Naturally, the established on-site hardware and software differs for each job-shop, thus making the creation of generally applicable solutions almost impossible. The biggest issue that needs to be solved is the discrepancy in data between the on-site software and the newly created DT of the production line. Manual data transformation and transfer is one of the options for the integration process, but it requires an experienced operator with a specific skillset to perform the actions necessary for seamless execution of this process. Automating the process of data integration between two systems helps alleviate the entry requirements for the DT technology implementation into a job-shop environment. The presented case study explores the possibility of using automated algorithms for production order data evaluation and processing which can be applied to other data types with minor adjustments to the methods proposed.

articleTitle: Bearingless Magnetic-Geared Motor Achieving Both Stable Magnetic Levitation and High Torque
abstract: In this study, optimization was conducted on five bearingless magnetic-geared motor models to investigate the structure that generates the highest torque, while ensuring that the suspension force equivalent to the eccentric force on the high-speed rotor (HSR). Furthermore, we investigated the suspension force ripples in the model with the best performance and evaluated the effect of skewing on reducing the suspension force ripples. It has been indicated that the model that has 8 HSR poles, 18 slots, 5 magnetized stator permanent magnets and 58 pole pieces has the potential to achieve both stable magnetic levitation and high torque.

articleTitle: Power Optimization of Hybrid Energy Harvestering from Mechanical Vibrations Using Piezoelectric and Electromagnetic Mechanisms
abstract: The rise of wireless sensing technologies and the Internet of Things has created a growing demand for efficient hybrid energy harvesting systems. This paper presents a necessary analysis of such a hybrid system, combining both piezoelectric and electromagnetic mechanisms to generate electricity from mechanical vibrations. This analysis is a crucial step for efficient implementation into industrial applications, ensuring that the system can meet practical performance requirements. The focus is on optimizing resistive loads for both circuits to maximize power output and improve energy conversion efficiency. A single-degree-of-freedom mathematical model is used to investigate the interaction between the mechanical, piezoelectric, and electromagnetic components. Numerical simulations are employed to identify optimal conditions for efficient energy harvesting, demonstrating that combining multiple energy conversion methods could enhance overall system performance.

articleTitle: Wearable System for Monitoring the Physical Conditions in Isolated, Confined and Extreme Environments
abstract: The intent of the article is to present a wearable system for assessing the physical fitness of team members in an ICE (isolated, confined and extreme) environment. A device enables recording, preprocessing and sending the measured MoCap and EMG data in real time to the PC. The system is composed of new HW, SW and ICT tools. Sensors of the system can be placed on selected body segments and in the exercise equipment structure to monitor motion and EMG data during exercises. The purpose of the unique system is to enable the examination and elimination of the effects of the ICE environment on various aspects of the subject's physical fitness. The system will enable the maintenance of sufficient physical activity and fitness of teams working or staying in ICE environments, thus increasing the safety and efficiency of teams' work and stay.

articleTitle: Design a Coffee-Making Process Unit Using Virtual Twin and Virtual Commissioning
abstract: This paper explores the design and implementation of a digital twin for machine handling the coffee-making process using a FANUC MATE 200iD/4s robotic arm. The digital twin was meticulously constructed from a CAD model provided by the robot manufacturer, ensuring precise replication of the robot's mass distribution and dynamic properties critical for accurate simulation. The production process covers various stages of coffee preparation, including grinding, tamping, placing the portafilter in the machine, brewing, and cleaning, all executed by a single, universally designed gripper. Both the gripper and other equipment, such as the coffee machine, were modeled in SolidWorks and validated in RoboGuide software using a virtual commissioning technique. The system allows continuous synchronization between the digital model and the physical robot, including updates on process variables such as waste bin status, coffee cup availability, and water levels. The chosen communication architecture, which utilized Modbus TCP for its flexibility, ensures dynamic adjustments throughout the process. The virtual commissioning process helped to optimize the robotic workflow, reduced errors, and significantly enhanced system efficiency. The findings confirm the important role of digital twin and digital commissioning methods in design an automation system, moreover, it shows the applicability of heterogeneous simulation software.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Aluminium Waste Sorting Process by Using Simulation Models
abstract: The article focuses on the optimization of sorting processes through the creation of simulation models. The research was conducted in a company involved in the processing of aluminium waste, specifically on the aluminium scrap sorting line. After an initial analysis and collection of real data, a simulation model was created, representing all the equipment and processes of the analysed sorting line. The simulation model was developed using Siemens Tecnomatix Plant Simulation software. To better illustrate the sorting processes, a graph was created to present the efficiency of the line's equipment. In the next step, a simple adjustment to the operation mode of the first screw conveyor was proposed within the simulation model of the original line, with the expectation of increasing the overall performance of the line. The evaluation of the results from the simulation run of the improved model showed a 40% increase in production volume. The research conducted through the creation of simulation models and experimentation represents one of the approaches to digitalizing manufacturing processes in the context of Industry 4.0. Further research will involve the creation of a digital twin of the analysed line, which will establish a real-time information connection between the actual equipment-components of the line-and its simulation model, with the aim of monitoring and subsequently managing the sorting processes.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of the Grouting Process Measurement Device with a Datalogger
abstract: Recording data from processes and activities has become essential for quality assurance and process verification, playing a pivotal role in research objectives. This necessity extends to the construction sector, where modern grouting waterproofing techniques are employed in tunnel wall renovations to protect structures from capillary water ingress, crucial for their longevity. Maintaining detailed grouting records is often required in practice, as these records provide insights into the substrate condition and grouting quality. This paper aims to design and implement a device that records physical data from the grouting process and stores it in a defined format on a microSD card. The paper outlines the problem analysis, identifies key input variables, and selects appropriate hardware components. The versatility of the proposed device allows for real-time monitoring of the grouting process and can be adapted to record the consumption of other substances, such as one or two-component paints. The proposal is structured into three main sections: an analytical part that addresses the problem analysis, a hardware part that discusses the selection of a suitable single-board computer and additional hardware, and a software section that explains the choice of programming language and the program's flow.

articleTitle: Selected Tools for the Analysis of Energy Harvesters Nonlinear Dynamics
abstract: This paper presents some possible ways to analyze and the influence of nonlinear characteristics on the dynamics and effectiveness of energy harvesting systems. Examples of tools such as the Lyapunov exponent, Poincaré sections, Impulse Excitation Diagram, and others are presented. Analysis of the impact of nonlinearity is helpful in designing and tuning such systems. In particular, the focus is on methods of imaging, describing and identifying chaotic and periodic motion zones and coexisting solutions.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Controller Tuning Methods for Typical Plant Types
abstract: This paper presents a contribution to fuzzy controller tuning. Fuzzy control is a control technology used in practice for years with excellent results thanks to their possible nonlinearity, which allows us to realize more complicated control strategies than classical PID controllers. This paper presents a new approach for fuzzy controller design and tuning based on a set of typical reactions. Its advantages are presented by comparison with a PID controller, tuned with the help of a standard tuning tool in a Matlab/Simulink environment. The set of typical plants from the area of agricultural application, including first-order plus time delay (FOPTD) and oscillating second-order plus time delay (SOPTD) plants was used to demonstrate the quality of fuzzy control with very good results.

articleTitle: Parametric Optimization of the Cooling Ducts of the PMSM
abstract: The paper shows an approach for optimizing the cooling ducts located in the housing of a synchronous generator. The machine consists of cooling channels for the inner air and outer water. The goal is to observe the influence of the dimensions of cooling channels on the temperature of machine components. Firstly, a sensitivity analysis is performed, and based on the results, an optimal design for the machine is selected. For this, an automated workflow was built in Ansys optiSLang connecting tools for changing the CAD geometry, creating a computational mesh, and solving the problem in Ansys SpaceClaim, Fluent Meshing, and Fluent, respectively.

articleTitle: Modelling a Non-Holonomic Mechatronic System Based on the Bicycle Chassis Principle
abstract: The controllability of mechanical systems of the non-holonomic type is currently one of the most discussed topics. The effects of limitations thus play an important role and, at the same time, become an automatic part of the movement. This paper discusses the constraints on the control accuracy of dynamical systems with non-minimum phase. These are limitations caused by the dynamics of the regulated system. Limitations due to unstable zeros and unstable poles will be clarified. Constraints caused by the pole and zero in the right half of the root plane were applied for the case of vertical stabilization of the chassis on the principle of a bicycle chassis with rear wheel steering.

articleTitle: Electrical Properties Measurement of Building Materials
abstract: This paper deals with the research of frequency dependence of capacitance, conductivity and relative permittivity of building materials. As the internal moisture content of a building material changes, the conductivity, relative permittivity and capacitance of the material also change. Using non-destructive dielectric measurements by means of the parallel plate method, the frequency dependence of these parameters can be measured in a humidification chamber for different moisture contents of building materials such as brick, plasterboard and wood. The measured data should provide realistic input parameters for electrostatic analysis and further experimental measurements of building materials in terms of absorption and propagation of air ions. Air ions occur naturally in the environment and represent a natural environment for humans. In indoor areas, their concentration is influenced by the absorption of building materials, which is highly dependent on the discussed electrical parameters.

articleTitle: Development of Integrated 3D Printing and Automated Embedding System
abstract: Numerous studies have focused on the embedding of objects through 3D printing, particularly in applications involving sensors and smart materials, which hold great promise for the Internet of Things (IoT). Embedding technology in additive manufacturing presents significant advantages for future innovations. However, conventionally it often requires interrupting the printing process to manually insert objects, leading to various inconveniences and uncertainty. This study focuses on automating the embedding of components during the additive manufacturing process. A novel embedding method for bottom-up vat photopolymerization printing has been proposed in this paper. In this approach, the embedded object is fixed at the bottom of the resin tank, directly beneath the model's cavity, prior to sealing. This setup allows for continuous printing, facilitating automation without the need for modifications to the printer's hardware and leveraging the benefits of the bottom-up printing system. A prototype system was designed that incorporates the bottom-up printer alongside a device utilizing SMT technology for component placement. This setup enables the automated embedding of objects during the printing process. The demonstration of the prototype system confirmed the feasibility of the proposed method, successfully achieving the automated object embedding.

articleTitle: Sensors Combinations as a Key for Effective Air Defence
abstract: The article focuses on the problem of aerial objects detection using various sensors and methods from the surface based air defence (SBAD) point of view. With the help of simulations it also proposes an optimal combination of active and passive radar and EO systems to ensure an adequate coverage of the Czech Republic. The analysis shows that the simulation of appropriate placement of sensors and their fusion can be beneficial not only for the real deployment phase but also for the better utilization of all the capabilities. The results of the simulations provide valuable insights for real deployment of sensors and SBAD assets, thus contributing to effective detection and protection of the Czech Republic's airspace. The article also contains number of pictures from the simulations of air strikes against selected objects in a simulation environment, where the possibilities of detection of air targets and the effectiveness of different sensor combinations are analyzed, including visualizations of radar coverage. Calculations of detection probabilities and effectiveness are also included. The aim is to show that there is no “silver bullet” solution and the choice of proper solution is usually use-case sensitive.

articleTitle: Real-Time Vision-Based Fault Detection System for FDM 3D Printing Using Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: We present a real-time vision-based fault detection system for Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) 3D printing, utilizing multiple You Only Look Once (YOLO) Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models-YOLOv4 Tiny, YOLOv5, YOLOv8, and YOLOv10-to identify defects such as blobs, cracks, spaghetti, stringing, under-extrusion, and warping. Unlike previous studies that use single models, our system integrates these YOLO variants to enhance detection accuracy and incorporates an adaptive learning module for continuous improvement based on real-time data. The system logs and displays faults on a live camera feed, significantly improving quality control in additive manufacturing. Comparative analysis shows that YOLOv8 achieves a 7% increase in detection accuracy and a 30% reduction in print errors. This novel integration of multiple YOLO models with adaptive learning advances automation and reliability in 3D printing.

articleTitle: An Integrated LCD Quality Assessment Flow based on the Integration of Image Processing, Ergonomics, and Machine Learning
abstract: In mass production, good and stable quality control and inspections are crucial. However, up to recent, LCD inspection process still highly relies on manually visual inspection from experienced works and could possibly be biased due to subjective judgement. Recently, automated optical inspection (AOI) has been adopted to LCD inspection for years, but defect classification and overall quality assessment still relies on human inspectors, which is inevitably biased by the physical and psychological conditions and a more objective manner and a rational flow should be developed based on computerized inspections. In particular, LCD inspections should accomplish both local defect classification and global mura defect quantification simultaneously and this represents a bottleneck for preventing LCD inspection automation. Thus, this work focuses on proposing a rational flow for addressing the above needs from classification and to quantify the possible LCD defects by using convolutional neural network and image processing to realize an objective defect classification based on both CNN and image thresholding. In addition, a novel quality evaluation index has also been proposed by adding the information of defected area, defected gradient, and average brightness of defected zone, to improve the existed SEMI index based on ergodic experiments. In summary, the flow presented in this work has achieved better and objective evaluations than that performed by human inspection. In the future, based on the flow outlined, it is expected that a more substantial defect classification and evaluation model suitable could be realized. This would benefit to LCD industries.

articleTitle: Adaptive Linear Control of a Cartpole Using Minimum Spiking Neurons Trained with Prescribed Error Sensitivity
abstract: In the search for highly parallel, power-efficient, and scalable chips for control applications, neuromorphic architecture has emerged as a promising candidate. Neuromorphic computing promises to address some of the the von Neumannian computing challenges, and computes using spiking neurons with adjustable synaptic delays that help match the latency of the controller with the system. However, learning in spiking neural networks poses a problem because of the non-differentiability of spikes. Although there are approximations like surrogate gradient decent for supervised learning, learning algorithms customized for spiking neural networks are required. Moreover, in order to design a compact, application-specific controller, the approximate knowledge of the number of neurons needed for a particular task is of importance, because the size of the chip depends on the number of neurons and synapse compartments on the chip. This work combines both of these needs and investigates the control performance on a cartpole with an adaptive controller by varying the number of neurons. The bob mass is varied and friction is added to the cart and the pole. First, the work shows the implementation of the Prescribed Error Sensitivity (PES) learning rule using a single neuron for the supervised learning of some standard functions, within the Neural Engineering Framework. Next, the work investigates the adaptive control of a cartpole against varying parameters, by progressively reducing the neuron number starting from 20 neurons, to arrive at a minimum number of spiking neurons, when trained with the PES rule. This knowledge is then used to run the adaptive controller on an FPGA board.

articleTitle: Application of Modern Approaches to Solving Diagnostic Tasks in Industry
abstract: Technical diagnostics is a separate scientific discipline focused on non-destructive methods of assessing the technical condition of objects and is one of the pillars of reliability and functionality of equipment. The definitions of technical diagnostics are based on various disciplines and standards, and technical diagnostics relies on the monitoring of diagnostic variables such as temperature, vibration, noise, and others. The paper further discusses the types of diagnostics, including vibrodiagnostics, thermodiagnostics, electrodiagnostics, etc., and their division into on-line and offline systems. The next section is focused on data evaluation, which is based on standards and methods, including frequency analysis and the use of artificial intelligence. The paper also discusses the use of cloud computing, edge computing, and risk theory, which can contribute significantly to the efficiency of diagnostic processes in the future. Finally, practical examples that have been solved at our department are presented. The first one is the use of the SIPLUS CMS1200 system for on-line vibration monitoring, which demonstrates its functionality and possibilities of use in industrial practice. The second example is the possibility of using neural networks in the processing and evaluation of measured data. The last example focuses on the application of risk theory in the evaluation of different diagnostic methods. The article aims to introduce the reader to the issues of technical diagnostics and then demonstrate possible approaches for practical solutions.

articleTitle: Geometry Optimization of a Highly Flexible Gradient Metamaterial Structure Using a Differential Evolution Algorithm
abstract: Gradient structures can offer great flexibility in parameter tuning, enabling the achievement of tailored mechanical properties for specific applications, and can even outperform their uniform counterparts. However, the design of such complex structures can be challenging, especially when many tunable geometric parameters are involved. To address this challenge, a simplified model that captures the main attributes and behavior of the structure can be employed. In this approach, a reduced number of parameters are optimized, while the remaining parameters are treated as constants throughout the structure. This also reduces the computational demands for simulating the structure with each iteration, thus accelerating the overall optimization process. A method for the geometry optimization of a highly flexible gradient metamaterial structure for the skin of a morphing aircraft wing's leading edge is proposed, utilizing a differential evolution algorithm. Initially, the basics of evolutionary algorithms and their representative, differential evolution, are introduced. Then, the flexible metamaterial skin with gradient bending stiffness, its simplified spring model, and the set of parameters for optimization are presented. Finally, the geometry parameters and the required acting loads are optimized using DE to achieve various deformed shapes that correspond to the morphing wing leading edge at different flight stages. Three levels of complexity of the optimized model are explored: a foundational version suitable for algorithm parameter tuning, an intermediate version for the optimization of geometric parameters and loading for one target shape, and an advanced version aimed at achieving multiple morphing shapes under different loading conditions.

articleTitle: Improving Safety Roads with LoRa Communication Devices: Features and Limitations
abstract: This paper presents a study with experimental tests toward a possible solution to increase safety in roads regarding crashed vehicles. The proposed solution system was developed combining GPS modules, accelerometers and LoRa modules for data transmission. Using LoRa technology for data transmission and other interface devices provides a very low cost solution with low energy consumption and a wide transmission range without the need for expensive satellites or mobile network antennas and or infrastructures. Using this solution, any crashed vehicle can send a warning message to all the nearby vehicles on the road with information about the exact location of the crash/collision. Nearby vehicles receiving this information can show up this information in the head up display (or infotainment or a simple alert sound) warning drivers to reduce speed and pay attention, allowing to avoid additional crashes and injuries and provide assistance eventually.

articleTitle: Case Study of the Influence of Linearity Uncertainty on the Applicability and Capability of CNC Machine Tools
abstract: Evaluation the capability of a CNC machine tool as a measuring device and the determination of TOL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</inf> according to ISO 22514-7:2021 is influenced by a number of factors. One of the important factors that enters into the calculation of TOL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</inf> is the root mean square deviation of linearity based on the Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). The present paper describes possible ways of evaluating the root mean square error of linearity obtained from measured data of accuracy and repeatability positioning a linear axis of a CNC machine tool according to ISO 230-2:2014. The evaluation of the accuracy and repeatability positioning is further implemented according to a modified measurement strategy and subsequent compensation of the linear axis of the machine. It is shown that the newly proposed modified measurement and compensation strategy of the CNC machine tool can lead to a reduction in the root mean square error of linearity and thus further contribute to increasing the capability and applicability of the CNC machine tool as a measuring device.

articleTitle: Autonomous Energy Harvesting – Based System for Honeybee Hive Monitoring
abstract: Minimizing energy consumption is a key aspect in designing modern IoT ultra-low power systems. An innovative autonomous sensor device, aimed at monitoring the strength of honeybee colonies, powered by using energy harvesting principles via the colony's waste heat, and comprising an array of temperature sensors to assess the size and thus the strength of the colony, is proposed in this work. The colony size is herein determined by measuring the difference between vacant hive areas and those occupied the honeybees. The aim of the work is to study methodologically, by employing artificial intelligence algorithms, the possibility of minimizing the number of the required temperature sensors, resulting in reduced energy consumption of the proposed sensor node. The necessary data is acquired via experimental measurements and thermal imaging and aimed at the highest possible accuracy in displayed thermal gradients. The results of the study will be instrumental in developing a functional autonomous hive monitoring system.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Downhill Regenerative Braking of Electric Vehicles from CAN Bus Data
abstract: Regenerative braking in electrified vehicles is particularly useful to recuperate energy when going downhill. The road load of a 2017 Nissan LEAF AZE-0 30 kWh was obtained and used to determine energy losses when going downhill. Data acquisition was performed through the vehicle CAN buses. The analytical losses caused by the road load were compared to the amount of energy not recuperated by regenerative braking. It was concluded that through the use of road load estimation, it was possible to quantify losses in regenerative braking with less than 10.2% error in cases where no friction braking is used. From the road load equation, it was identified that the regenerative braking efficiency can be improved significantly by reducing vehicle speed. The results were compared to those from a 2019 Hyundai KONA Electric 64 kWh, from which it was shown that a combination of stronger regenerative braking during coasting and a higher peak regenerative braking power across a range of vehicle speeds can improve the round-trip regenerative braking efficiency.

articleTitle: Implementation of Artificial Intelligence in Internet Search
abstract: The article presents an evaluation of the application of artificial intelligence in searching and retrieving information on the Internet. Potential sources of information were identified, procedures for searching Internet resources were developed, and methodologies for analyzing and presenting results were proposed. Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods applicable to identifying the semantics of texts, i.e. understanding the meaning and context contained in sentences and documents, were applied. Webcrawlers and a Python library were used to prepare the data. The Bert-Base-Uncased and Bert-Large-Uncased models were analyzed in detail, determining the generation times and probabilities of the correctness of answers, as well as the relevance parameter, as evaluations of whether the generated answer agrees with what the user wanted to search for.

articleTitle: The Influence of Approximating the Mechanical Characteristics of a Hyperelastic Vibration Amplifier on Its Dynamic Properties
abstract: The results of the model studies presented in the authors' works indicate that incorporating an additional oscillator in the energy recovery system, functioning as a mechanical amplifier for the external load, positively influences the energy recovery capability. From a theoretical standpoint, its design can be based on a linear oscillator. However, much better results are achieved when its mechanical properties are represented by nonlinear characteristics. In the case of nonlinear oscillators, harmonic components are excited over a wide range of variability, allowing for the possibility of obtaining a solution characterized by a stable orbit encircling all potential wells. The computer simulation results presented in this paper illustrate the influence of approximating the mechanical characteristics of a hyperelastic vibration amplifier on its dynamic properties, which may facilitate the subsequent analysis of an energy harvesting system based on a hyperelastic mechanical vibration amplifier.

articleTitle: Simplified 6DoF Flight Model of the Missile
abstract: Flight simulation of air-to-air and ground-to-air missiles is usually performed with the use of rigid-body six degrees of freedom equations of motion. Such model can be further simplified by two assumptions: firstly, the missile is symmetric in both horizontal and vertical plane and secondly, the roll motion of the missile is automatically stabilized and thus the roll dynamics is excluded from the simulation. These assumptions allow simplifications in formulation of the Equations of Motion and the reduction of the total number of required aerodynamic parameters. This paper presents a mathematical formulation of such model. The first part of the paper introduces the development of Equations of Motion for symmetric missile utilizing the locked roll axis. In the second part, two most common approaches for expressions for aerodynamic coefficients are explained together with the simplifications arising from the symmetry and locked roll axis. Finally, the third part of the paper proposes basic guidelines for determination of the missile aerodynamic characteristics with the use of the component build-up method.

articleTitle: Design of a Smart Condition Monitoring System of Equipment in the Production Process
abstract: The core of the publication is the design of an automated evaluation system for monitoring the state of production equipment, and machines, and the state of the production process by monitoring selected parameters of the manufacturing equipment with an additional sensory subsystem. The idea is to process the data at the level of production process management, so the edge computing technology principles are used. The work is divided into several steps including the description of the monitored process, the selection of key parameters, the design of the method of processing the measured data, and data storage along with the design of the communication infrastructure for the entire system. Example tests in the form of experimental operation on the device under laboratory conditions of the proposal are included. The output of the system can be used as a basic tool for the predictive maintenance process, while the condition state of the equipment is available via an interactive IoT application.

articleTitle: Human 0, MLLM 1: Unlocking New Layers of Automation in Language-Conditioned Robotics with Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Language-conditioned robotics has seen tremendous growth in frameworks that aim to improve the success rates of robots acting upon the environment according to free-form language instructions. However, most existing frameworks leverage a human in the loop to assist with critical functions. Humans are mainly involved in ensuring that a human-requested task is feasible, resetting the robot when it diverges from achieving the requested goal, and deciding if it has completed the task. As human involvement limits the scalability of language-conditioned robotics, we propose automating these human functions through Multimodal Large Language Models in the Loop (MLLM-IL). We conduct experiments leveraging multimodal large language models, specifically OpenAI's GPT-4, and Google Gemini, to evaluate their potential in automating crucial functions. The introduced new layers of automation include analyzing task feasibility, assessing task progress, and detecting task success. We investigate how different factors, including the choice of LLM, image resolution of the input images, and the structure of the prompt, affect the performance of the LLMs in achieving the target functions. Results show significant zero-shot success with feasibility analysis accuracies exceeding 90%. Our work demonstrates the immense potential of utilizing MLLM-IL to complement existing frameworks in language-conditioned robotics, opening the space for a wealth of new applications.

articleTitle: Comparison of Three-Winding Transformer Model Extraction Using FEMM and COMSOL Multiphysics®
abstract: This research focuses on simulating a transformer using electromagnetic field solver software: FEMM and COM-SOL Multiphysics®. These tools are used to simulate and extract the model of a three-winding transformer. The primary objective of the extracted model is to predict key magnetic parameters, such as leakage and magnetizing inductances. These inductances play a critical role in switch-mode power converter topologies, ensuring proper operation and achieving high efficiency through zero-voltage or zero-current switching. In this study, the transformer, based on an ER28/14/11 core, is simulated using both FEMM and COMSOL, with the resulting models compared to each other and experimental measurements. FEMM is a free, 2D solver, while COMSOL is a commercial, 3D solver. This research aims to evaluate the feasibility of using the non-commercial FEMM tool to simulate complex transformer core shapes. Transformations of the E, ER, and ETD core types for simulation in both 2D axis-symmetric and planar problem types are also proposed.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of an AdBlue® Injection System and Implementation on a Dual-Fuel (Diesel/LPG) Engine
abstract: Euro 6 Diesel vehicles use Diesel Particulate Filters (DPF) and Urea-Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) to reduce particulate matter and NOx emissions. Accurate exhaust gas NOx and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathrm{O}}_2}$</tex> measurements are critical to assess aftertreatment system effectiveness. Tests on a 2019 Dacia Stepway, equipped with DPF and SCR, revealed unreliable ECU data for NOx and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathrm{O}}_2}$</tex> sensor readings obtained from an automotive scan tool. To address this, CAN messages from NOx sensors were captured and calibrated using a laboratory-type UniNOx (Continental) sensor. From the data gathered it was possible to implement an AdBlue aftertreatment system on a laboratory diesel engine, controlled via a developed injection scheme, to optimize NOx reduction through precise AdBlue injection. Details of the developed system are detailed in this paper. Chassis dynamometer testing utilizing the test vehicle showed consistent 24ppm tailpipe NOx levels, regardless of engine load, whilst the laboratory setup achieved stable value of 30ppm whilst minimizing ammonia slip. During active DPF regeneration on the test vehicle, higher exhaust temperatures challenged the SCR system, briefly increasing NOx emissions. Oxygen concentration differences between engine-out and tailpipe gases allowed soot oxidation quantification, matching DPF soot reduction reports from the scan tool.

articleTitle: Body Performance Analysis with Machine Learning and ANOVA Methods
abstract: Detection of body performance with artificial intelligence using body data can provide a precise and objective evaluation of individuals' physical abilities. Artificial intelligence models can create personalized training programs and development plans by learning from large data sets. This can help athletes and fitness enthusiasts optimize their performance and reduce their risk of injury. Additionally, health professionals and coaches can make more effective and targeted interventions by making data-based decisions. In this study, it was aimed to predict the performances of athletes using body data. A dataset containing 13,393 rows of data in total was used. There are four classes in the dataset and they represent performance levels. Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Gradient Boosting (GB), Random Forest (RF) machine learning methods were used to classify the data. The cross validation method was used to objectively evaluate the results of the models. Confusion matrix and performance metrics were used to analyze the performance of the models. Classification successes and other performance metrics obtained as a result of the classification of the models were used to compare the performances of the models. The highest classification success of 74.5% was obtained from the ANN model. The lowest classification success was obtained from the RF model with 69.6%. ANOVA was used to examine the effects of the features in the dataset used on classification. The effects of the features were analyzed and their importance level was determined. It is thought that the proposed models can be used in applications by using them in performance analysis.

articleTitle: Coverage Path Planning for Robotic Laser Surfacing Applications Based on 3D Scanning
abstract: Robotic laser surfacing technology is gaining popularity in many industrial branches and there is a need for an autonomous system combining the robotic laser surfacing technology with the rapidly evolving area of industrial machine vision. This paper presents the tool path trajectory planning module of our software designed to control a 9 DoF robotic work cell with a laser surface modification equipment based on scanned data from a robot-mounted 3D camera. Our method respects the specific requirements of the laser surfacing technology as well as the possibilities and limitations of the physical system containing an industrial robot on a linear rail and an additional two-axis servo positioner. This paper describes the whole technique of our scanning-based robot navigation system including the workpiece scanning, model creation, coverage trajectory planning, simulation and execution of the robotic laser surfacing process.
